answer.rationale: The temporal correlation between the release 2 hours ago and the 90-minute climb in p99 write-path latency strongly suggests the release is the cause. Memory b1 documents a prior instance where a rollback cleared an error spike cleanly without customer impact. Rolling back preserves all in-flight writes (the rollback completes without dropping transactions) and avoids the risk of adding capacity into a potentially broken build or triggering regional failover during peak settlement load. Circuit breakers and read-replica routing do not address write-path latency. Given exactly one intervention, rollback is the highest-confidence action to restore the write path while preserving customer writes.
